verdict.root_cause: cartservice's Redis calls are held at a fixed ~300-311ms floor per command, and that wait is the failure. Traces show every sampled cart operation spending effectively all its time in a single Redis leaf span (HGET or HMSET) with the gRPC handler under 1ms of self time, reads and writes equally affected, tightly banded rather than long-tailed [tr_e39e15c5c9b5]. A uniform floor with near-zero variance is the signature of interposed egress delay, not server-side contention, and the change log records exactly that artifact on this path: a traffic-shaping container attached to the cart-service network namespace injecting fixed egress delay, plus a REDIS_ADDR port override, both by platform-automation [tr_cb567cd9d301]. Both are logged as reverted ~1.3-1.6h before onset, so the likeliest reading is that the shaping rule persisted in the pod's network namespace after the injector was detached, or was re-applied without a log entry. Upstream symptoms follow mechanically: latency multiplies per cart round-trip to ~910ms frontend POSTs and ~640-690ms PlaceOrder spans while every other checkout dependency stays in single-digit ms [tr_e39e15c5c9b5].
verdict.reasoning: The mechanism is waiting, not failing: no span is error-marked or deadline-terminated and all trees complete [tr_e39e15c5c9b5]; cart logs show uninterrupted request handling with no connection or startup lines [tr_3dbeb26e86c6]; checkout logs show complete order flows with advancing queue offsets [tr_13dc5ab103dc]. That eliminates crash-loop, image-pull and hard-down readings. The traces localise the delay to one hop in all 10 traces, with a floor-shaped distribution rather than a tail - the discriminator between injected delay and queueing. checkoutservice alerted loudly but its errors are intermittent (~1% mean, ~6% peak, no sustained departure) and the metric has no per-dependency dimension, so it noticed rather than caused [tr_15edc01dfe65]. cartservice's error-ratio series is empty in both windows and contributes nothing [tr_6c9d77963f97].
open_questions: Whether the shaping rule actually stopped when the injector was detached - nobody inspected the live pod's netns or tc rules.
Onset is unattributed: the trace window has no pre-onset comparison, so the ~300ms floor may predate 06:28:45 and imply a different trigger.
redis-cart itself was never queried, so a genuinely slow Redis server cannot be excluded on its own telemetry.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself is slow (server-side or network-path degradation) with no injected component involved.
alternatives.why_not: A loaded or contended Redis produces variance and a latency tail; the observed band is a near-constant floor across reads and writes [tr_e39e15c5c9b5], and no Redis-side telemetry was gathered to support it.

alternatives.root_cause: The REDIS_ADDR override to a non-default port left cart talking to a degraded or proxied endpoint.
alternatives.why_not: The override is logged as reverted to its prior unset state 1.3h before onset [tr_cb567cd9d301], and a wrong address would more likely produce connection errors than uniformly successful 300ms commands [tr_3dbeb26e86c6].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the container rebuilds cartservice's network namespace, where a residual tc egress rule would live. If that is the mechanism, Tempo traces of the same shapes as in tr_e39e15c5c9b5 should show HGET/HMSET leaf spans fall from the ~300-311ms band to single-digit ms, frontend cart POST roots from ~910ms to under ~100ms, and PlaceOrder roots from ~640-690ms to ~20-40ms. Loki cart-service lines should resume at prior cadence with no startup errors.
proposal.if_wrong: Traces after the restart still show HGET/HMSET pinned near 300ms with sub-ms handler self time: that falsifies the stale-netns reading and points at redis-cart itself, which was never queried. Also falsifying: latency drops then snaps back to ~300ms within minutes, implying re-application by platform-automation. Note cartservice has no usable Prometheus span-metrics (tr_6c9d77963f97), so confirmation rests on Tempo and Loki only; if no comparable trace is sampled inside the window, treat this as unconfirmed rather than fixed.
proposal.risk: I chose restart over the named config_revert because the only recorded prior config is REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6380, already reverted 1.3h before onset; restoring it would point cart at a likely-wrong port and could break cart persistence outright. Restart's own risk: it discards cartservice's in-process state and drops in-flight cart gRPC calls, so some carts in mid-checkout may error; if the delay is actually in redis-cart or an external injector, the restart buys nothing and costs a brief outage while burning the 'process state' hypothesis.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice for the seconds it takes to recreate. Its inbound callers - frontend (cart view/add) and checkoutservice (GetCart, EmptyCart in PlaceOrder) - see connection resets, which will surface as a short error spike on top of checkoutservice's already-elevated ratio (tr_15edc01dfe65) and as failed cart POSTs for loadgenerator traffic. No other checkout dependency is touched.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting within 15 seconds along the cart/checkout/frontend call path is a coherent multi-service failure, not a single dismissible warning. The fan-in pattern starting at cartservice suggests a shared downstream dependency, but that prior is weak and nothing rests on it.
